chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from the one who mentioned it, from Umar ibn Muhammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever prays the morning prayer and says, before shaking his knees, ten times,'

There is no god except Allah, Alone, there is no partner for Him. For Him is the Kingdom and for Him is the Praise. He gives life and causes death, and He is Ever-Living and will not die. In His Hand is the good, and He is Able over all things.
And in the evening (he says) similar to it. A servant would not meet Allah, Mighty and Majestic, with a deed superior to his deed, except for the one who comes with a similar deed.

key_terms.بِيَدِهِ الْخَيْرُ: In His Hand is the good (divine power over all good)
key_terms.رُكْبَتَيْهِ: His two knees (referring to the bowing position in prayer)
key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: There is no god except Allah (declaration of monotheism)
key_terms.لَهُ الْمُلْكُ: For Him is the Kingdom (divine sovereignty)
key_terms.يُحْيِي وَ يُمِيتُ: He gives life and causes death (divine attribute)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite after morning and evening prayers?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith highlights the spiritual efficacy of dhikr immediately following the fard prayers, a practice emphasized by the Ahl al-Bayt to secure divine favor before concluding the ritual. The specific attributes invoked—such as Al-Hayy (The Ever-Living) and Al-Qadir (The Almighty)—underscore Allah's absolute sovereignty and power over life and death, reinforcing the concept of Tawhid in daily worship. This act is elevated to the status of a supreme deed, suggesting that consistent adherence to this specific remembrance yields profound spiritual rewards comparable to other major acts of worship.
